subject: Streaming parser degradation impacting PeakRetail - urgent
messages:
From: Alex Burns <alex.burns@peakretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sally Monroe <sally@peakretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in p99 latency + errors on our live checkout stream

Neha / Redwood team —

We're seeing a steady increase in p99 request latency and a spike in 5xx errors on the live streaming checkout endpoint since yesterday (~03/17 22:00 UTC). This is affecting our high-concurrency peak lanes and causing timeouts in our client SDK.

Attached a short trace we pulled from our edge (support_trace_20260318.log) and a p99 summary (slo_p99_report.pdf). Key points:
- Error rate went from 0.2% to 2.4% at peak.
- Latency p99 jumped from 450ms to ~2.3s.
- Failures appear correlated with sessions using the latest PeakRetail SDK 1.4.7 and streaming mode.

Can you triage and loop in engineering? We need an ETA because this is blocking our midweek promotions.

—Alex
Alex Burns
Head of Integrations, PeakRetail
Attachments: support_trace_20260318.log (text), slo_p99_report.pdf (pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Engineering Oncall <ops@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in p99 latency + errors on our live checkout stream

Forwarding PeakRetail traces — high priority.

Quick summary for oncall: customer reports p99 latency from ~450ms to >2s and 10x error rate increase tied to client SDK 1.4.7 in streaming mode. Attached logs from customer and their p99 report.

Immediate asks:
1) Can infra/serving confirm any backend resource pressure or recent kernel/kernel-flag changes?
2) Can client-platform validate if there are known regressions handling fragmented header frames or streaming parser reassembly in recent releases?
3) If this is a client-side integration issue, we need a mitigation plan (hotfix, rollback, or routing them to a non-streaming endpoint).

I'll keep PeakRetail on a short leash but avoid alarming execs until we have root cause. Sean/Jonas — can you take lead? Vanessa, I'm cc'ing you for account coordination and potential commercial remediation.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: support_trace_20260318.log, slo_p99_report.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in p99 latency + errors on our live checkout stream

Thanks for the ping — digging in now. Initial triage notes:

- No obvious backend CPU/GPU saturation across the serving fleet in the time windows PeakRetail called out. Memory and IO look nominal.
- We see a pattern of failed stream reassembly on our ingress for a subset of connections. Errors: "parser: header_reassembly_timeout" and "stream: unexpected-trailer" in the same trace segments.
- These failures line up temporally with SDK 1.4.7 sessions from PeakRetail (their trace includes user-agent: PeakSDK/1.4.7).

Hypothesis: recent changes in the client SDK's streaming framing (smaller prefix fragments) expose a race in our streaming parser that mis-associates partial header frames when packets arrive interleaved. The parser ends up dropping fragments and signalling an error to the request path, which manifests as higher p99 and 5xx rates.

Short-term mitigation options:
A) Ask PeakRetail to fall back to non-streaming fallback endpoints (simple HTTP request/response) — minimal platform changes but client impact.
B) Deploy a patch to the ingress parser to increase the reassembly window and make header coalescing more tolerant — lower-risk patch, but needs careful perf validation.
C) Gate behavior by user-agent: treat PeakSDK/1.4.7 connections as tolerant mode while we roll a more permanent fix.

I recommend option C as a quick containment (we can roll a per-client routing rule) and option B as the engineer-approved fix with a follow-up release. I'll start an experimental branch for the parser tolerance changes and capture perf timings.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Attachments: (none)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Burns <alex.burns@peakretail.com>, Sally Monroe <sally@peakretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T07:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming parser degradation impacting PeakRetail - urgent

Hi all — status update for PeakRetail and execs.

What we've done:
- Applied a per-client routing rule yesterday at 23:40 UTC to treat user-agent PeakSDK/1.4.7 as "lenient reassembly". That reduced observed error rate from 2.4% -> 0.35% in their traces over the next 2 hours.
- Deployed an experimental parser branch to a small canary pool. The branch increases header reassembly window and adds additional checks to avoid dropping interleaved fragments. Canary showed no CPU regression on small loads; more load testing in progress.

Next steps (timeline):
- Today (03/19): finish load validation of the parser patch and run a synthetic with mixed small-fragment bursts. Target: 6-8 hours.
- 03/20 morning: if green, push patch to global ingress with a config flag to monitor effect.
- 03/20 afternoon: ship a minor SDK advisory to PeakRetail recommending 1.4.6 rollback if they cannot accept lenient routing, plus a scheduled SDK patch 1.4.8 to align framing semantics (this will be coordinated with the PeakRetail integration team).

Commercial note: PeakRetail runs a committed usage contract (D-4729). Vanessa, recommend we prepare a courtesy credit for the outage window to keep relationship warm. Will defer to you on amount.

I will keep Alex/Sally updated hourly until we have full remediation.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering
Attachments: internal_canary_report-0319.txt (summary)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: CEO Office <ceo@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Burns <alex.burns@peakretail.com>, Sally Monroe <sally@peakretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec briefing: PeakRetail streaming parser incident (summary + ask)

Folks — quick executive summary and recommended ask for approval.

Incident summary:
- Timeline: 2026-03-17 22:00 UTC — 2026-03-19 01:00 UTC (peak impact window).
- Impact: PeakRetail saw p99 latency regressions (~450ms -> ~2.3s) and a temporary 5xx error rate spike from 0.2% -> 2.4%. Roughly 4.5% of their sessions during peak were affected.
- Root cause (current): Client SDK 1.4.7 changed streaming framing semantics (smaller prefix fragments) which exposed a race in our ingest streaming parser that led to partial header drop and reassembly failures.

Actions taken:
- Temporary per-client lenient reassembly routing applied (reduced errors to ~0.35%).
- Parser patch in canary; load validation ongoing.
- Coordination with PeakRetail on SDK advisory and scheduled SDK patch (1.4.8) to stabilize framing.

Ask (for exec decision):
- Approve a customer courtesy credit for PeakRetail for the impacted window. Suggested starting point: 15% usage credit for the billing cycle related to D-4729. Vanessa — any commercial input?
- Approve an expedited security/QA slot for the parser patch to be prioritized in the 03/20 release train. This will require an extra 2 QA cycles and a short rollback plan.

If approved, I will send a customer-facing remediation note with the credit offer and a timeline for the permanent fix.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Contact: neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183
